title: Microsoft Plugin Architecture: reuse the core, govern each host
decision: Standardize skills and MCP; govern compatibility and ownership per host.
summary: Bottom line: standardize skills and MCP, then govern compatibility and ownership for each host.

claims.text: Three host routes use different delivery contracts: Cowork uses Microsoft 365 app packages; declarative agents use MCP or API actions; GitHub Copilot uses plugin packages.
Skills and MCP configuration can be reusable, while manifests, discovery, authentication and client-specific components remain host-specific.
Cowork packages skills and connectors in a standard Microsoft 365 app package.
Microsoft 365 declarative agents support MCP and REST API plugins as in-agent actions; REST API tools are defined in the plugin manifest.
GitHub Agent Plugins 1.0 ports skills and MCP configuration across compatible clients; client-specific components and legacy plugins remain supported.

sections.title: 1. Choose the host route
sections.body: Cowork uses a Microsoft 365 app package. Declarative agents use MCP or REST API actions. GitHub Copilot uses plugin packages with portable and client-specific parts.
sections.speakerNotes: Evidence: the three selected official sources, retrieved 2026-10-06. Decision implication: name the host and package contract for every portfolio item; do not describe these routes as interchangeable.

sections.title: 2. Reuse the core, not the wrapper
sections.body: Reuse skill logic and MCP configuration where tested. Keep authentication, manifests, discovery and client-only components inside each host package.
sections.speakerNotes: Evidence: Cowork skill portability, declarative-agent MCP/API behavior, and GitHub Agent Plugins portability and legacy support. Interpretation: the reusable layer should be separated from host packaging and operations.

sections.title: 4. Govern a small portfolio
sections.body: Assign one owner per capability and service. Publish a host compatibility matrix, version each package, and add routes only when demand justifies lifecycle cost.
sections.speakerNotes: Proposed operating model, grounded in the documented route and compatibility boundaries. No source prescribes an enterprise org chart or ROI target.

voice.narration:
Bottom line: standardize skills and MCP, then govern compatibility and ownership for each host.

Cowork uses a Microsoft 365 app package. Declarative agents use MCP or REST API actions. GitHub Copilot uses plugin packages with portable and client-specific parts.

Reuse skill logic and MCP configuration where tested. Keep authentication, manifests, discovery and client-only components inside each host package.

REST API actions remain supported in declarative agents. Agent Plugins 1.0 adds portability, while legacy GitHub Copilot plugins continue to load.

Assign one owner per capability and service. Publish a host compatibility matrix, version each package, and add routes only when demand justifies lifecycle cost.
